paper_title: 1.4 Million Open-Source Distilled Reasoning Dataset to Empower Large   Language Model Training
caption: Difficulty distribution of the data entries. Most of the dataset entries are classified as Medium (51.8%) or Hard (25.7%). A smaller proportion falls into the Easy (11.2%), Very Hard (6.5%), and Very Easy (4.7%) categories.
model_annotation: The pie chart displays the "Distribution of Difficulty" across five distinct categories. A legend located in the top-left corner provides the category names along with their absolute numerical counts: Medium (725,892), Hard (360,137), Easy (157,053), Very hard (91,576), and Very easy (65,332). Category labels and their corresponding percentages are positioned directly outside each slice around the perimeter of the chart, rather than being placed inside the segments. The largest slice is "Medium," colored light red, representing 51.8% of the total. Moving counter-clockwise, the next slice is "Hard" in light blue at 25.7%, followed by "Easy" in light green at 11.2%, "Very hard" in light orange at 6.5%, and "Very easy" in light purple at 4.7%. Visually, the segments are arranged in descending order of size, progressing counter-clockwise starting from the top vertical axis. None of the individual slices are visually emphasized, offset, or exploded.
